question: What do official sources establish about the 2017 Timalan and Pasong Camachile watershed studies, and can they support a distinct Pasong Camachile river lead or fish claims?

sourceReviews.title: CvSU inks two new MOA with DENR-PENRO
sourceReviews.access: Official CvSU February 2017 newsletter PDF, page 2, reviewed online.

findings.projectTitle: The newsletter names a biophysical and socio-economic characterization, vulnerability assessment, and integrated watershed management plan for Timalan and Pasong Camachile River Watershed projects.
findings.projectTiming: It says the projects would run for seven months starting February to July 2017 and describes comprehensive profiling whose results would be used for management plans.
findings.deliverables: The notice does not link or reproduce a completed plan, fish checklist, sampling protocol, station coordinates, taxonomic identifications, or GIS boundary. It is evidence of a project announcement, not proof of completion or fish results.

sourceReviews.title: Environmental Impact Statement: Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX) Project, Cavite Section
sourceReviews.access: Official EMB-hosted EIS full text reviewed online; no local PDF retained.

findings.riverIdentity: The EIS explicitly names Pasong Camachile River among rivers traversed by the project and reports a Pasong Camachile River Basin catchment of 10.22 square kilometres. It describes Pasong Camachile and San Juan Main Stream as components of the wider San Juan River Basin.
findings.fishEvidence: The previously reviewed EIS fish paragraph is general study-area/multi-river context and does not assign a taxon to Pasong Camachile River or a fish station. No Pasong-specific fish assertion is supported.
findings.geometry: The source-reported catchment area and watershed map are not a reusable vector boundary or channel geometry; no geometry was extracted.

sourceReviews.title: Cavite Ecological Profile 2024
sourceReviews.access: Official provincial profile PDF text reviewed online for its river-course and watershed-table excerpts; no local copy retained.

findings.courseNarrative: The profile describes Pasong Camachile River as starting from Santiago, passing San Gabriel, and connecting with San Juan River. This source narrative does not establish a surveyed centerline or complete route.
findings.watershedGrouping: The profile separately lists a Camachile-Ylang-Ylang River Watershed at the larger watershed-table scale. Similar naming alone does not establish that this grouping is identical to the Pasong Camachile River or its separately named source-era basin.
findings.fishEvidence: The reviewed river-course and watershed excerpts provide no Pasong-specific fish inventory or sampling information.

boundedSearch.outcome: The search located the official CvSU 2017 project announcement, official Cavite ecological profile excerpts, and the previously reviewed official EMB EIS. It did not locate the completed watershed management plan, a fish-specific report or dataset, a station-to-taxon crosswalk, or reusable vector geometry.
limits: This bounded public web search does not cover unpublished project files, institutional library holdings, local archives, or non-indexed attachments.
Failure to locate the deliverables does not establish that the project was not completed or that fish are absent.
The neighboring Imus baseline's aggregate fish summary for several watershed studies has no named species or waterbody-by-taxon allocation and is not transferred to Pasong Camachile or Timalan.

rightsReview.decision: Retain source metadata and minimal attributed research facts only. Do not reproduce the newsletter, EIS, profile tables/maps, or any underlying project deliverable without item-specific reuse review.

nextAction: Locate and review the completed CvSU/DENR-PENRO 2017 Timalan and Pasong Camachile watershed plans or associated fish-survey deliverables through a public repository route. Verify species identification, survey date, method, station-to-waterbody attribution, and reuse terms. Keep watershed polygons distinct from river channels and do not submit an access request without separate authorization.

sources.supports: Official CvSU newsletter announcement of the Timalan and Pasong Camachile watershed projects, participants, stated period, and planned profiling.
Official EIS naming Pasong Camachile River, reporting its source-era catchment context, and describing it within the wider San Juan River Basin; its broad fish context is not assigned to this river.
Official provincial profile's source-described Pasong Camachile course and distinct Camachile-Ylang-Ylang watershed table entry.
